evaluation.positioning_hook: A panic-ridden Uber driver with crippling anxiety finally gets a Tinder match, then has to fight his own mind to make it to the date and send the message that could change his life.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The emotional premise is instantly legible and relatable, especially for viewers who know dating-app dread and social anxiety. The challenge is that the script is very small in scale and highly internal, which narrows the commercial lane even as it gives the piece a clear audience.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands fast: Jacob gets a match, spirals through a catastrophic fantasy, and the whole piece is about whether he can act despite his anxiety. The title motif and repeated 'Hey' pattern give the premise a clean, memorable spine.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Jacob is sympathetic and specific, with enough contradiction to hold attention: self-deprecating, hopeful, vain, and deeply fragile. Maria is more of a catalyst than a fully dimensional counterweight, so the character engine is strong for a feature but not especially expansive.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script takes a familiar anxiety premise and gives it a formal gimmick that feels personal rather than decorative, especially in the looping 'Hey' nightmare and the cereal/TV/phone motif. It is bold in concept and execution, though still operating inside a recognizable indie-psychological framework.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The piece moves cleanly from match to date to panic spiral to reset, and the fantasy sequence escalates effectively. Because the runtime is built around one emotional beat, the momentum is more cumulative than propulsive, with the ending functioning as a release rather than a plot turn.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The anxiety visualization is fresh in a way that immediately communicates the character's inner life, and the 'Hey' motif gives the script a simple, sticky organizing idea. It feels like a short-form or micro-feature concept that is novel without being opaque.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The world is specific in small details — basement apartment, Uber work, pharmacy, pub, Tinder, Ativan — but it functions mostly as a container for Jacob's interior state. There is texture, but not much social or institutional depth beyond the protagonist's immediate environment.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The tone is distinct: anxious, surreal, and lightly comic in the way ordinary objects become threatening. The repeated sound design and visual motif create a recognizable register, even if the piece stays close to one emotional frequency.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: There are seeds of deeper material around self-image, medication dependence, and the gap between fantasy and action, but the script keeps those ideas close to the surface. It reads as a concise emotional exercise more than a layered world with hidden chambers.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: This is almost entirely a one-character piece, with Maria, the waiter, the pharmacist, and Dr. Watson functioning as brief pressure points rather than an ensemble engine. The script lives or dies on Jacob's internal experience, not on recurring relationship dynamics.

lead_characters.name: Jacob
lead_characters.demographics: Male, late 20s, morbidly obese, urban working-class, anxiety disorder implied, aspiring writer.
lead_characters.hook: Jacob is a basement-dwelling Uber driver with a writer's ego and a wrecked self-image, the kind of guy who can joke about being a 'professional couch potato' while quietly unraveling over a first date. He is funny, self-aware, and deeply avoidant, which makes his smallest victory feel hard-won. The script is built around his inner life: the fantasy of being wanted versus the terror of being seen.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of a performance like Philip Seymour Hoffman in Capote or Jesse Plemons in The Power of the Dog — a role where internal shame, humor, and vulnerability do the heavy lifting. It gives an actor a full emotional close-up role with physical specificity, comic timing, and a clear transformation beat.

lead_characters.name: Maria
lead_characters.demographics: Female, 20s, student and retail worker, psychologically literate, socially confident.
lead_characters.hook: Maria is the match who becomes Jacob's imagined hope and his real-world test. She is warm, teasing, and observant, but the script keeps her intentionally partial — more a mirror for Jacob's self-worth than a fully explored romantic lead. That restraint makes her function cleanly as the pressure point in the story.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an actor the grounded, disarming energy of a Zoey Deutch or Haley Lu Richardson performance — the ability to make a few scenes feel emotionally loaded without overplaying them. The showcase is precision: playing charm, concern, and subtle recalibration in very little screen time.

lead_characters.name: Waiter
lead_characters.hook: The Waiter is a functional but important pressure valve in Jacob's pub meltdown, the ordinary stranger who becomes part of the panic spiral. He is not written as a full character so much as a social obstacle, which is exactly why the scene works as a public humiliation beat.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of contained, scene-stealing support role that lets an actor play straight-man realism against an escalating lead performance, similar to the best service-industry beats in indie comedies and dramas. The opportunity is to anchor a key panic sequence with calm, reactive authority.

lead_characters.name: Pharmacist
lead_characters.demographics: Adult, any gender, service counter worker.
lead_characters.hook: The Pharmacist is the bureaucratic face of Jacob's crisis, a deadpan obstacle who turns a medication emergency into another humiliation. The role is small but useful because it externalizes the stakes of Jacob's dependence on Ativan without needing exposition.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a crisp character-actor beat in the vein of the best dry, procedural support turns — the kind that lets an actor land a scene with economy and timing. The showcase is controlled deadpan against a spiraling lead.

lead_characters.name: Dr. Watson
lead_characters.demographics: Adult, any gender, physician or therapist voice only.
lead_characters.hook: Dr. Watson exists as an off-screen authority figure, the voice Jacob reaches for when his anxiety spikes and the pharmacy fails him. The character is more function than presence, but the call gives the script a credible medical anchor without leaving Jacob's subjective space.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a voice-only or minimal-screen-time role that can still register if cast with a distinctive, reassuring presence. The showcase is authority without overexplanation.

lead_characters.name: Neighbor
lead_characters.hook: The Neighbor is a tiny but effective trigger in Jacob's paranoid soundscape, a casual 'Hey' that lands like a threat. The role is brief, but it helps the script turn ordinary social contact into psychological pressure.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of micro-role that gives an actor a memorable beat through timing alone, similar to the best one-line pressure-cooker moments in indie features. The showcase is making a small moment feel loaded.

casting_characteristics: Lead requires a late-20s male actor who can carry anxiety, self-deprecation, and physical specificity.
Supporting roles are age-flexible and serviceable as character parts.
No twins, no special physical doubles, no child casting.

locations.interior_exterior_ratio: Mostly interior with limited exterior street beats

technical.vfx_details: No visual effects required beyond basic editorial transitions and subjective POV styling.
technical.sfx_needs: Sound design emphasis for breathing, looping 'Hey' audio, and subjective panic cues.

rights_flags.detail: Tinder is named and shown on Jacob's phone.
Uber is referenced as Jacob's job.
Ativan is named on the medication bottle.

platform_fit.recommended_lane: Streaming or premium cable indie drama
platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model: specialty theatrical, streamer original, or festival-to-platform acquisition.

budget.note: Contemporary, contained, and mostly interior with no VFX, no stunts, and only a handful of simple locations. The main cost driver is sound design and performance coverage, not production scale.

casting.note: Jacob is the whole movie, and the role requires an actor who can play shame, humor, and panic without losing audience sympathy. Maria also needs enough warmth and intelligence to make the date feel emotionally real in very little screen time.

development.note: The script is built around one psychological turn, so the buyer conversation will focus on whether the concept sustains feature length and whether the ending delivers enough lift after the fantasy reset. The formal motif is clear, but the piece is highly dependent on execution and performance.

comp_set.why_it_comps: Shares the autobiographical, anxiety-forward romantic-comedy-drama lane where personal vulnerability is the engine and the lead's emotional honesty is the selling point.

comp_set.title: Eighth Grade
comp_set.why_it_comps: Matches the painfully specific social-anxiety perspective and the way ordinary interactions become high-stakes internal events.

comp_set.title: The Skeleton Twins
comp_set.why_it_comps: Comps on the indie-drama tone where depression, humor, and emotional collapse coexist in a compact, actor-driven package.

comp_set.title: Swiss Army Man
comp_set.why_it_comps: Shares the surrealized inner-life approach and the willingness to turn psychological distress into a formal, highly ownable visual language.

audience_target.primary_audience: Adults who respond to intimate, emotionally honest indie dramas about anxiety, dating, and self-image.
audience_target.demographics: 18-44 skewing slightly female, urban/educated, streamer and festival audience, strong overlap with character-driven indie buyers.

budget_tier.note: Contemporary contained feature with a small cast, a few practical locations, and no VFX or stunt burden.

lane_fit.detail: This sits naturally in the lane of intimate, performance-led films that can travel on concept, tone, and a strong lead turn. The formal anxiety motif gives it a slightly higher-concept hook than a standard relationship drama, which helps it stand out in the indie marketplace.

ip_potential.detail: Standalone feature with a closed emotional arc; no clear sequel or spinoff vector.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The anxiety motif is instantly ownable.
strengths.what_it_means: That gives the film a clean marketing handle and a clear reason for buyers to remember it after one read. It will appeal to execs looking for a small, high-concept emotional piece that can be sold in a sentence.
strengths.evidence: The repeated 'Hey' motif, the looping TV audio, the alphabet magnets, and the cereal spelling all externalize Jacob's panic in a consistent visual system.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Jacob is a strong actor role.
strengths.what_it_means: A lead this specific can attract talent who want a showcase rather than a generic romantic lead, which is valuable in the indie and streamer space. Casting directors and managers will see a performance piece with humor, shame, and physicality.
strengths.evidence: His self-description as a 'professional couch potato,' the Ativan dependency, and the pub meltdown all give the actor multiple registers in a short span.

strengths.what_it_means: That keeps the project accessible to indie financiers and makes it easier to package without name-heavy attachments. A director can make this with a small footprint and still have a distinctive formal hook.
strengths.evidence: The story stays in a basement apartment, a pub, a pharmacy, a street, and a bedroom with no VFX or action burden.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The fantasy reset is emotionally efficient.
strengths.what_it_means: The structure gives the film a built-in climax without needing a large plot machine, which is attractive for buyers looking for contained, character-led material. It also gives the ending a clear emotional release that can play well in a festival room or streamer browse.
strengths.evidence: The date disaster is revealed as Jacob's imagined nightmare, then the story returns to the beginning and lands on the real act of sending the message.

whats_special.headline: This is a contained, production-light indie with a memorable psychological hook and a lead role built for an actor showcase. The formal 'Hey' motif gives buyers a clean marketing angle, while the small-location footprint keeps the project inside a very financeable lane.

items.area: The feature engine is extremely narrow.
items.detail: The script is essentially one anxiety beat stretched across a feature frame: match, fantasy date, panic, reset. That makes the buy highly dependent on tone and performance, and it will be read as a short-film concept unless the buyer is already sold on the formal device.

items.area: Maria is more catalyst than character.
items.detail: She functions primarily as the object of Jacob's hope and fear, with limited independent texture beyond being a psychology student who works retail. Buyers will notice that the romantic counterweight is intentionally thin, which keeps the story focused but also limits the relationship engine.

items.area: The ending lands on emotional release, not plot escalation.
items.detail: The final beat is Jacob sending the text and calming his breathing, which is satisfying on a character level but modest as a feature climax. That makes the script feel intimate and complete, but it also caps the commercial lift for buyers expecting a bigger third-act turn.

items.area: Brand names will need a legal pass.
items.detail: Tinder, Uber, and Ativan are all named on the page, so business affairs will want to decide whether they stay as clearances or get generalized. None of them are fatal, but they are real clearance items rather than incidental background.

issues.headline: The main friction is scale: this is a very specific, very contained psychological piece, which is exactly why it feels fresh and exactly why some buyers may read it as short-form in feature clothing. The other conversation is packaging — Jacob is a strong role, but Maria is intentionally light and the branded references add a small legal layer on top of an already narrow commercial lane.
